actual_scope: Quotient the BIT local word's eight-axis ambient by the annihilator of a kernel subspace K of dimension k, then re-pad the full-ambient image with all k freed axes so every helper stays physically D_I8 and the tensor block stays 7. The submitted word uses K = span{150, 102, 255} (k = 3, quotient width 5). One dimension reaches 0.0124, two 0.0218, three 0.0322, four falls back to 0.0175; every replay-valid three-dimensional kernel prices identically. This moves the BIT supplier from 0.003464248972 to 0.032249423394893 (+830.92%, and +160.05% over this package's own one-dimensional frontier base 0.012401086416). The outer kappa does not move here: with the complex supplier at 0.015637149091, min(complex, BIT) is 0.015637149 and the complex side binds.
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for derivation, implementation, checking and writing; no independent human or formal-kernel review claimed.
author: Douglas Colkitt, with substantial AI assistance
bottleneck_link: The BIT supplier bound the outer kappa until this quotient; the local paid rank mass is the term the ambient frame lattice controls directly, and a k-dimensional quotient removes up to k ranks from every MOVE whose destination meets the kernel. After this the BIT has 2.06x of headroom over the complex supplier, so the complex side is the constraint.
evidence: BIT supplier kappa 0.003464248972 -> 0.032249423394893 (+830.92%). verify.py replays the pinned source word (reproducing the declared local bill {1:1323,2:1342,3:79,4:44,5:102,6:11,7:19}) and the quotient in both directions: 24,305 ADDs, 9 COPY episodes, all 661 endpoints and all arbitrary input columns exact, paid profiles identical, helper starts at ground and finals at dim 8, ambient dim 8, kernel basis independent. scan_kernels.py prices the dimension ladder; 445 of 455 sampled solids are valid and all price identically.

scope_change_reason: The card asks for a replacement H2/K interface. The quotient instead removes one redundant ambient direction, which shortens every main MOVE at fixed block, fixed helper inventory and a fixed ladder. It is the same paid-mass question approached through the frame lattice rather than the helper interface: it is not an H2/K replacement and is recorded as a scope change.
